valhallaSpike.scope: Native builder on existing synthetic offline source fixture. No DEM or regional capacity measurement.
conclusions: The builder preserves useful native topology, physical pairs, source way IDs and pedestrian directions.

Deleting foot=yes from two source ways produces byte-identical final tiles. Final tiles alone cannot preserve explicit versus inferred permission; separate source evidence or a builder change would be required.
A blocked pedestrian gate has pedestrian-allowed incident edges but pedestrian-blocked node access. An edge-only exporter would introduce a false connection.
Documented Python GraphUtils lacks bulk adjacency/access/source export. Midpoint Actor.locate probes recovered all fixture edges but are not a lossless general export interface.
Missing elevation is flagged; sentinel node elevation is not a valid measured profile. Populated profiles, partial DEMs and regional performance remain untested.
Do not adopt Valhalla as a drop-in compiler: source evidence and a reliable bulk exporter would still need custom implementation. This does not establish that the current Python compiler scales.

selectionDecision: The user requested all meaningfully different routes without a count cap. A later audit of 2,056 options showed duplicate circuits across starts, overly broad fitted-map selection and road-heavy walks. Global similarity grouping, explicit preset rectangles and adjustable road limits replace those behaviors; see route-quality-review.json.
